title: DC Sources & Circuits

notes.heading: 1. KCL, KVL, Superposition & Star-Delta (Y–Δ) Conversions
notes.proseLatex: Kirchhoff's Current Law ($\sum I = 0$ at a node) expresses charge conservation; Kirchhoff's Voltage Law ($\sum V = 0$ around a closed loop) expresses energy conservation. Superposition applies to voltages and currents in linear bilateral networks (deactivating independent voltage sources to SHORT circuits and independent current sources to OPEN circuits — NEVER deactivate dependent sources, and NEVER add component powers $I^2 R$ by superposition!). Equal resistors convert cleanly via $R_\Delta = 3 R_Y$.

keyFormulas.label: Current/Voltage Divider & Symmetric Y–Δ Rule
keyFormulas.latex: $I_1 = I\,\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2},\qquad V_1 = V\,\frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2},\qquad R_\Delta = 3 R_Y\;\text{(symmetric)}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Apply current divider (opposite branch R in numerator!) and star-delta collapse.

notes.heading: 2. Thévenin, Norton & Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
notes.proseLatex: Any linear two-terminal network reduces to a Thévenin voltage $V_{\text{th}} = V_{\text{oc}}$ in series with $R_{\text{th}}$ (or Norton current $I_N = I_{\text{sc}} = V_{\text{th}}/R_{\text{th}}$ in parallel with $R_N = R_{\text{th}}$). A variable resistive load $R_L$ extracts MAXIMUM power when matched to the source resistance $R_L = R_{\text{th}}$, yielding $P_{\max} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4 R_{\text{th}}}$ at exactly $50\%$ efficiency! (Notice $50\%$ is efficiency AT maximum power transfer, NOT maximum efficiency — $\eta = \frac{R_L}{R_L + R_{\text{th}}} \to 100\%$ as $R_L \to \infty$!).

keyFormulas.label: Thévenin-Norton Duality & Maximum Power Transfer
keyFormulas.latex: $V_{\text{th}} = I_N R_{\text{th}},\qquad R_L = R_{\text{th}} \implies P_{\max} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4 R_{\text{th}}}\;(\eta = 50\%)$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute Vth, Rth, maximum load power, and distinguish max power from max efficiency.

examples.problemLatex: A linear DC network has open-circuit voltage $24\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $6\text{ A}$ at terminals $A$-$B$. Find $R_L$ for maximum power transfer and $P_{\max}$.

notes.heading: 3. First-Order RC & RL DC Transients & Steady-State Shortcuts
notes.proseLatex: Capacitor voltage $v_C(t)$ and inductor current $i_L(t)$ CANNOT jump instantaneously ($v_C(0^+) = v_C(0^-)$ and $i_L(0^+) = i_L(0^-)$). In DC steady state ($t \to \infty$), an ideal capacitor acts as an OPEN CIRCUIT and an ideal inductor acts as a SHORT CIRCUIT! Every first-order transient obeys $x(t) = x(\infty) + [x(0^+) - x(\infty)]e^{-t/\tau}$ with time constant $\tau_{RC} = R_{\text{th}} C$ and $\tau_{RL} = \frac{L}{R_{\text{th}}}$ (reaching $63.2\%$ of total change at $t = \tau$ and $>99\%$ by $5\tau$).

keyFormulas.label: Universal First-Order Step Response & Time Constants
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Evaluate t = 0+ continuity, t = infinity open/short equivalents, and RC/RL time constants.

examples.problemLatex: An uncharged $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected across $100\text{ V}$ DC through $R = 50\text{ k}\Omega$ at $t = 0$. Find time constant $\tau$ and $v_C(0.5\text{ s})$.

workedExamples.problemLatex: A linear DC network has open-circuit voltage $24\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $6\text{ A}$ at terminals $A$-$B$. Find $R_L$ for maximum power transfer and $P_{\max}$.
An uncharged $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected across $100\text{ V}$ DC through $R = 50\text{ k}\Omega$ at $t = 0$. Find time constant $\tau$ and $v_C(0.5\text{ s})$.

wbjeebTraps: Notice $\tau_{RC} = R\cdot C$ whereas $\tau_{RL} = L / R$ (do NOT write $L\cdot R$!).

Charging an uncharged capacitor $C$ from a constant DC source $V$ through ANY resistance $R$ stores $\frac{1}{2}CV^2$ in the capacitor and ALWAYS dissipates an equal $\frac{1}{2}CV^2$ as heat in $R$ (50% charging efficiency regardless of $R$!).
Superposition NEVER applies directly to power ($P = I^2 R$ is non-linear): compute net $I = I_1 + I_2$ FIRST, then square!
